title: Equipment & trading
summary: Item qualities, trading, equipment access and reward systems.
body:
Classic crafted and quest equipment

More stock armor and jewelry now offer offensive, defensive and casting effects. The list covers149 item families across all four existing qualities. The effect strength is the same at each quality. Existing effects and stats stay unchanged.

New glove effects give 10% or 20% melee haste. A stronger item haste effect takes priority. New shoulder effects add 5 or 15 ATK. New head and foot effects add 1 or 2 HP or mana per tick. Dodge and parry effects use the strongest matching worn effect.

Damage and affliction focuses use Nightcap scaling. Their 20% endpoint contributes 200% before other modifiers. Spell-level and spell-type limits still apply. Duplicate item and augment focuses do not add together. An existing stronger focus retains its strength.

Custom augments, weapon procs and healing strength stay unchanged. Recipes still produce their existing quality. Enchanted jewelry and its same-name unenchanted version are different items; only the enchanted items below gain effects.

Classic augment stacking

A level-50 paladin with eight Ascended Prismatic scales gained 960 HP and 960 mana. Eight Healing or Magic scales supplied 80 Healing Amount or Spell Damage. Improved Dodge I on the Dodging scale, Gauntlets of Fiery Might and Efreeti War Shield shares one +10 worn modifier. A mixed set can combine a type-7 chest scale with one type-22 raid trophy.

Classic raid gear effects

Across all four qualities, the Robe of Inspiration gains Mana Preservation II, the Apothic Robe gains Extended Range II, the Blue Crystal Staff gains Improved Damage II, and the Warhammer of Divine Grace gains Improved Healing II alongside its existing attack proc. The Efreeti War Shield and Gauntlets of Fiery Might each grant Improved Dodge I. Two matching worn dodge effects give one bonus. Matching gear focuses use the strongest eligible source.

Classic Prismatic scales

At level 50, combine White Dragon Scales and a Black Sapphire (Healing), Red Dragon Scales and a Fire Emerald (Magic), or White Dragon Scales and a Star Ruby (Dodging) in a standard Jeweler’s Kit. Use type-7 sockets in head, arms, wrists, hands, chest, legs or feet. The Reforging Box upgrades plain scales in groups of 3, 4 and 4. At Ascended, Healing and Magic grant 120 HP, 120 mana, 10 Healing Amount or Spell Damage and their rank IV focus. Dodging grants 120 HP, 120 mana, 5 damage shield and Improved Dodge I. Nine stock Classic augment families also receive rounded stats across all four qualities.

Find ordinary equipment with the Loot finder, browse Hunt rewards, or compare an upgrade in the experimental Build Lab.

Player trading and duplicate items

Trade formerly NO DROP and NO TRANSFER items, already-attuned gear, bags, their contents and augments. LORE restrictions are disabled, so duplicate ownership is allowed. Inventory capacity, temporary-item expiration and Pet Armor restrictions remain. Equipment eligibility still depends on your held classes and the remaining item requirements.

Item name colors

Usable item names show their quality: Regular is green, Polished is blue, Exalted is purple, and Ascended is orange.

These colors appear in item inspection, Advanced loot and Bazaar seller listings. Hunt rewards use orange for Ascension.

Native equipment restriction warnings still apply. A quality color does not change which items you can equip.

Polished, Exalted, and Ascended loot

Eligible dropped equipment and bags can appear in three stronger custom tiers. Their health, mana, defenses, and offensive stats scale by item family.

Ordinary eligible equipment and bags now roll 20% Polished, 5% Exalted and 1% Ascended, leaving 74% Normal when all variants exist. These chances apply per eligible item drop, not per kill. Already generated loot is not rerolled. Zone-hunt and dungeon rewards retain their separate rates.

Augments in50 Classic zones; gear in the original48

Any unowned, killable NPC in an enabled augment zone can roll its augment, including guards, named and quest NPCs, killable merchants and scripted combat adds. Player-owned/charmed pets, mercenaries, swarm pets, protected noncombat actors and restored corpses do not reroll. Native corpse ownership and encounter access still apply. Augments roll at 1.5%; approved native equipment sources keep their separate 0.5% chance and level/night restrictions. Qualities remain Base60%, Polished30%, Exalted8%, Ascension2%; no guaranteed drop or pity counter. Zone rewards.

Six armor locations for heroic augments

Eligible Base and tiered head, arms, hands, chest, legs and feet armor gains one type-22 socket, preserving existing sockets. Zone augments add stats and heroic attributes; item level requirements still apply. At level 50, every two effective heroic INT from these socketed augments allows one more point of item Spell Damage, up to +30; heroic WIS does the same for Healing Amount. With the current 750 cap, either can reach 780. Extra cap room only helps when you have enough of the actual bonus.

Upgrade matching rewards

#zoneforge uses three Base copies for one Polished reward, then four Polished for one Exalted or four Exalted for one Ascension. Artisan Veyra’s reusable Reforging Box also upgrades four identical Polished or Exalted copies, including eligible ordinary tiered gear. The box also accepts three identical eligible Normal/Base copies for Polished; higher recipes stay at four. Read Item upgrades for inputs, restrictions and the two distinct top-tier names.

Heroic stats on Ascended equipment

Ascended gear and Ascended epics add heroic stats on top of their improved base stats. This describes the existing equipment tiers; the new zone rewards have their own heroic stats at each quality.

Gear bonuses for casters and healers

Eligible direct damage spells and procs add effective Spell Damage once. Each ordinary DoT tick adds half the effective bonus, rounded down, independent of duration. Healing Amount retains percentage healing and its existing HoT distribution. Each item-bonus total has a 750 base cap; eligible Hunt augments can raise it to 780 at level 50 when enough actual bonus is equipped. On spell gem casts and activated AA spells, each heroic INT point adds 0.1% direct damage and each heroic WIS point adds 0.1% direct healing. Procs, combat skills, DoT ticks and HoT ticks receive neither heroic multiplier. The separate Bard area-DoT route retains its native behavior.

More room for core stats

The normal core-stat cap is raised to 425, with heroic stat effects handled separately.

Ascended summoned equipment

Eligible summoned gear becomes Ascended when a matching version exists. The supported Paladin and Cleric summoned-hammer families have zero merchant resale value at every quality, including items you already own. Summoning does not bypass spell or item-level requirements.

More room in your bags

Buy bags up to 40 slots, with base prices from 10 to 7,500 platinum. Merchant price adjustments and each bag’s capacity and contents restrictions still apply. Free trading does not reduce expensive bag purchase prices.

Better payouts for ordinary loot

Boosted merchant payouts remain in place for ordinary loot. Formerly NO DROP items use the fixed one-platinum payout below instead of those price modifiers.

One platinum for formerly NO DROP items

Ordinary merchants and #sellall pay exactly 1 platinum per physical item from the eligible formerly NO DROP pool. Five stack units pay 5 platinum; a charged object pays 1 platinum total. Purchase prices have a one-platinum floor. Merchant previews can differ from actual payment. Zone-hunt rewards, dungeon rewards and the supported divine summoned-hammer families have no merchant resale value.

Bulk selling from the command or merchant window

Use #sellall to sell eligible carried items without targeting a merchant, or use the merchant window’s Sell All button. Containers, food, drink, spell reagents and casting focus items are kept. Zero-value items, including zone rewards and the supported divine summoned hammers, are skipped. Sales are immediate and can include valuable gear. Bank anything you want to keep first.

Winged Helm of the Dawn

A custom Paladin helmet with an installed appearance for visual testing. Earn this helmet through Camil’s Vigil of the Dawn, now in live testing.

Wear gear for your whole build

Ordinary equipment recognizes all held classes. Class-matching wearable items and augments allow all playable races; deity, level, slot, weapon and augment restrictions remain. See equipment eligibility.

Dungeon completion rewards

Raid and Grind dungeons have 24 shared reward designs and three exclusive Raid designs for each of the 21 released dungeons. Grind grants Normal; Raid grants Polished or Ascended. These permanent, tradeable, non-lore items have zero merchant resale and no existing forging recipe. Their bags have up to ten slots and 100% weight reduction.

Item click reuse

Items without an explicit shared reuse group keep their own cooldowns without locking unrelated abilities. Copies of the same item share reuse; explicitly grouped items still share their group. Existing saved waits retain their expiry. See the cooldown update.

Reviewed Ascended values

Supported numeric fields on 131 Ascended items now follow inspected THJ Legendary references. These families use per-item values rather than one universal multiplier. Some values are lower than before; original effects and existing sockets remain.

Starter upgrades and dungeon progression

Approved starter families use smaller steps: Bronze chest armor has 6, 7, 8 and 9 AC across Normal, Polished, Exalted and Ascended. Bronze Long Sword has 4, 5, 6 and 7 damage at fixed delay 32. Cultural armor is excluded from this retuning. Comparable Normal dungeon rewards remain stronger.

Earned melee and pet equipment

Selected items gain sympathetic healing, combat procs or received-healing support. Healing, Runic and Hastened Fragments of Truth and Bloodfrenzy Core have earned boss routes; later-era bosses still require their normal access. Bloodfrenzy Core is a power-source item, while the original Bloodfrenzy remains a weapon. New sockets do not bypass augment compatibility.

Ascended class-armor quest rewards

Crafted, Lambent, Darkforge, Ivy Etched and Totemic quests now grant existing Ascended versions of their 37 reviewed armor rewards. Substantial class-armor quests qualify even when repeatable; cheap/basic hand-ins stay excluded. Materials and quest requirements remain. Already-owned armor is not automatically converted. Scope and live testing.

The Vigil of the Dawn — live testing

The Winged Helm of the Dawn is earned through Camil’s Vigil of the Dawn. Its existing stats and sockets remain unchanged. Chapterhouse also awards three miniboss items, six final Raid variants and a four-quality augment. Read the quest guide and reward catalog.

Quest ingredients and item quality

Normal-item quest requirements accept Polished, Exalted and Ascended versions of the same item. Shakrn Meadowgreen in South Karana accepts an Aviak Charm of any ordinary quality plus two Star Rubies for Ascended Crafted Gauntlets, following the current class-armor reward policy. Ingredients are consumed; their quality does not upgrade the configured reward. Exact Normal inputs are used first when both are offered. Explicit quality requirements, reforging recipes and separate epic, hunt and dungeon catalogs retain their own rules. Quest hand-ins and task delivery support the change; in-game acceptance testing remains open.

How ordinary item stats scale

The update uses unmodified stock ProjectEQ as an approximation of standard EverQuest, then preserves the exact researched values where available. It changes 143,332 existing tier definitions across 47,809 eligible ordinary families. Normal items, the 209 starter families, custom Hunt/dungeon rewards, augment families and quest-only epics keep their existing treatment. Families that exceed native stat limits are excluded for review.

Polished and Exalted receive one-third and two-thirds of the increase from Normal to Ascended. These intermediate formulas and extrapolation beyond the screenshots are Nightcap tuning choices. Attack and sparse utility fields use stock values unless an exact observed override applies. Existing effects, sockets, delays, equip rules, loot routes and owned items are preserved.

The Ashen Compact — live testing

The Ashen Compact is an installed level-50 Shadow Knight helmet campaign in a curated Kael expedition. Its paired server and client release is available for testing; full encounter, rendering and balance acceptance remain open.

The Warhelm of the Ashen Compact uses the Paladin helm budget with INT replacing WIS. It requires a held Shadow Knight class. Its new enclosed Classic appearance requires the paired client update.

Persistent player listings — live testing

The Commonlands player market is installed for live testing; native search and buying still need player verification. Its supported permanent items and stacks remain listed while the seller is offline. It has stricter posting requirements than direct player trading, including empty bags and exactly recoverable saved item data. Market instructions and restrictions.

Paladin weapon grips — live testing

Paired October28 update: fully exit EQ and use launcher Play to install release2026102801. It repairs the stale client definition that could leave SoulFire two-handed after a 1HS message. Shield use and rendered swing checks remain open for player testing.

The assessed stats are installed for live testing. Ascended SoulFire uses 26/30 in 1HS or 46/45 in 2HS with Accuracy 10; Ascended Avenger uses 30/30 or 66/44 with Accuracy 15; Ascended Defender uses 36/30 or 72/40 with Accuracy 25. Avenger adds 1 point and Defender adds 3 points of shield block with an eligible shield in 1HS. Defender also gains improved healing and heroic wisdom, with its proc available at level 45. Grip changes preserve augments and saved charges. The one-handed grip stays primary-only. Shield abilities and augments can affect which grip deals more damage.

The SoulFire, Fiery Avenger and Fiery Defender quests award their Ascended versions directly. No extra essence or platinum is required for Defender. Owners of an original Defender can use the free Epic Forgemaster exchange, preserving its grip and customizations. There is no automatic inventory conversion. Meet each quest's faction and ingredient requirements.

Change grip out of combat and casting. Remove the shield before returning an equipped weapon to 2HS; augments must support the destination type. SoulFire's heal click is replaced by the grip toggle. Return to 2HS before reforging eligible copies. The grip is saved per item, including Bazaar transfers; generic links and type filters describe the base 2HS definition. Full native gameplay and balance acceptance remain pending.

All top-quality augments, drop zones and secondary specialties — live testing; gameplay acceptance remains open.

Power Source training — Not released

A separate combat-XP path for supported item families is in development. A training item occupies the Power Source slot and grants no equipment benefits there. Existing loot qualities, stats, drops and Reforging Box recipes remain. Power Source training preview.

Equipped bonuses in Inventory Stats

Open Inventory → Stats to see your current server-calculated equipped bonuses and caps. Values update automatically while the tab is open. Shield Block and the relative Dodge modifier have their own rows. Scroll down for item spell-haste and mana-preservation potential and worn Faerune. Focus values are the best equipped item potential before spell limits; they are not a promise for every cast. The separate Shielding row remains melee damage reduction. Damage/healing caps include earned headroom. Bagged and training items give no bonus.

After fully exiting EverQuest, use launcher Play to install signed update2026110604 (client0.13.4). A missing or stale server reply shows “--”. #augstats remains a diagnostic fallback. Native sizing, scrolling and gameplay acceptance remain live QA.

Shield Block shows one total including equipped augment bonuses. The strongest augment shield-block bonus applies; two +1% copies still give +1%. Shielding remains a separate damage-reduction stat.

Last Lantern campaign armor

Earn eight personal armor pieces over the level20–50 Adventure Journal, with legal woven, leather, chain or plate fits and earned refits. Exact stats and chapters. Live testing; harder endgame loot remains worthwhile.

Stat augments and equipment icons

Ordinary stat augments keep the equipment's own icon and appearance. Genuine cosmetic ornaments still change appearance. If an older item displays an augment icon, report the item name and slot to the owner; do not destroy augments as a workaround.

Combat stats and heroic attributes in Inventory

The main Inventory tab shows AC, MIT, AVD, ATK, DMG and HEAL above your attributes. MIT is the mitigation AC rating used by the server. AVD is the server defense rating used for the hit check, not the item Avoidance bonus or a percentage chance to dodge. Auto indicates an automatic-avoidance effect; sitting and other attack checks still apply. AC remains the conventional client display. ATK is your attack rating; DMG and HEAL are Spell Damage and Healing Amount bonuses, not damage or healing per cast.

Each attribute has a green current value, a white /cap and a yellow/gold signed heroic total. The cap is the actual server cap, including heroic allowance. Heroics are already included in the current value and cap: do not add the yellow number again. No heroic bonus displays as +0. Missing or stale server totals show -- while refreshing.

Fully exit EverQuest and use normal launcher Play to install the latest client update. The main Inventory tab has no scrollbars. The wider information column keeps the normal font readable. The separate Stats tab retains equipped secondary bonuses, focus potential and the single Shield Block total. This release is in Live testing; player checks of placement, gear/buff refresh, zoning and skin reload remain open.

Classic raid augments drop from 25 named bosses. Choose one level-50 chest trophy for damage, healing, defense or resource recovery.

Classic sympathetic clicks

Any class can use these two Ascended items. Only the Ascended copies grant the buffs. You can also make them with the ordinary Reforging Box recipes.

  1. Equip the item.
  2. Right-click it to start the two-second cast.
  3. After the cast, put your usual gear back on.

Both buffs can stay active together. Use the same item again to refresh its buff.

  • Sympathetic Strike I. A lava elemental in Solusek’s Eye drops the Runed Lava Pendant (Ascended). Cast a single-target direct damage spell from a spell gem. The base mana cost must be at least 10 before mana preservation. If the spell lands fully, the target takes one extra hit. An eligible lifetap deals extra damage without increasing its healing.
  • Sympathetic Healing I. A frenzied ghoul in Lower Guk drops the Moonstone Ring (Ascended). The ring keeps Extended Range II. Cast a single-target direct heal from a spell gem. The spell must have a base mana cost above zero. The same target receives one extra heal. If a worn sympathetic focus delivers a direct heal on this cast, the worn effect takes precedence.

Each bonus equals 5% of the largest eligible hit or heal from the cast. Round down to a maximum of 48. A 40-point heal gives 2 extra before overheal. A 960-point hit gives 48 extra before target protections.

Area spells, spells with a duration and partial resists cannot activate either buff. Pet casts, item clicks and triggered casts also give no bonus.

Worn ATK on stock gear

The 135 families below gain ATK as they improve in quality. The item window shows its full value. If your character is below an item’s recommended level, the server reduces its contribution before adding it to your worn ATK. The base worn cap is 250. Applicable item, spell and AA bonuses can raise the cap.

For example, an Ascended Armguard of Shadows lists 53 ATK. It contributes up to 44 at level 50 and 53 at its recommended level of 60. If your other gear already reaches the cap, equipping more worn ATK adds zero. The Inventory ATK rating also includes skills, STR and other bonuses.

Remove an augment

Buy a Perfected Augmentation Distiller from Della in the East Commonlands tunnel if your augment needs a distiller.

  1. Keep the distiller in your inventory and empty your cursor.
  2. Open the equipment window for the socketed item. Select the augment and choose Remove.
  3. Move the returned augment from your cursor to your inventory or another compatible socket.

Removal uses one distiller when required. The equipment stays in its slot. The separate Destroy action destroys the augment.

Healing power and casting speed

Improved Healing increases healing power. Spell Haste reduces the cast time of qualifying spells. See fast healing in melee for the Minor Healing and Light Healing bonus, Djarn's Amethyst Ring and interruption guidance.

Focus effects on Classic drops

Classic dungeon and raid drops offer more spell haste, healing and mana preservation. The following items have these effects in Normal, Polished, Exalted and Ascended quality. The focus is the same at each quality. Existing stats, click effects and worn effects remain.

Spell Haste reduces eligible cast times by 15%. Improved Healing provides up to 20% more healing, and Mana Preservation provides up to 10% lower mana cost. Only the strongest eligible item or augment focus in each category applies. Wearing two healing focuses does not add their percentages.

Ranks I, II and III cover spell levels through 20, 44 and 60. Existing decay above those limits remains. Spell Haste also requires a base cast time of at least 1 second for I, 2 seconds for II, or 3 seconds for III. These are limits on the spell, not your character level.

Keep a HasteII option for Light Healing: its 2 second cast is too short for HasteIII. HasteI can cover Minor Healing. A higher focus rank does not help every spell. Focuses reduce the time exposed to attacks; they do not prevent interrupts or stuns. See fast healing in melee.

Healing focus no longer adds unintended mana preservation. Healing strength is unchanged.

Equipment ornaments

The Ornament Artisan stands beside the Epic Forgemaster in the East Commonlands tunnel. Hand over one spare item with no coin and leave space in your pack. The exchange permanently consumes the donor and gives you its appearance as a statless ornament. Remove augments first. Customized items are returned.

Use a type 21 socket on head, chest, arms, wrists, hands, legs or feet. Use type 20 for compatible held items, shields or bows. The item you wear keeps its own stats and effects. Both wrists can be socketed, and the first wrist supplies the displayed texture. Eligible corpses share a 1% chance to drop one random ornament. Every zone draws from the same 14,768 designs.
